title: Jack Osbourne's SPARK TV Opens as Pentagon Drops Biggest UFO Archive in History
excerpt: Jack Osbourne UFO streaming platform SPARK TV has launched as the US government releases its largest-ever UAP disclosure -- 375 declassified Pentagon files through PURSUE since May 2026. The paranormal streaming platform covers UFO disclosure, consciousness research, and investigation content now
content:
Jack Osbourne has launched SPARK TV streaming platform, dedicated to UFO disclosure, paranormal investigation, and consciousness research — arriving at the precise moment the US government has made more declassified UAP data publicly accessible than at any point in the country's history.

Since May 2026, the Department of War's Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters — known as PURSUE — has released five tranches of declassified records, totaling 375 individual documents, videos, and photographs spanning cases from 1947 through 2026. The government itself has created, for the first time, a massive publicly accessible library of verified anomalous phenomena records — and SPARK TV is the first streaming platform built explicitly to serve the audience now trying to make sense of them.

"I'm gonna be doing a new podcast for them, actually, in the UFO space, so that's kind of where I'm putting a lot of my energy right now," Osbourne told outlets in August 2026. He described the platform's ambition as aggregating the growing audience for UFO and paranormal content "to one destination," and bringing "a bit of Hollywood cachet" to a space that has historically been, in his words, "kind of indie, a little bit cheaper looking, a little bit kind of scrappy."

SPARK TV is available now at sparktv.ai, and on the Amazon Appstore app listing, Google Play, and Apple platforms.

What Is PURSUE, and Why Does It Matter for Streaming?

To understand why SPARK TV exists when it does, it helps to understand what the US government has been releasing this year. PURSUE — the Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters — was established by a Trump executive order in February 2026 directing federal agencies including the Pentagon, FBI, CIA, State Department, and Executive Office of the President to identify and release UAP-related records. Full legal analysis of the ODNI's implementing guidance was published by DLA Piper in August 2026.

Five tranches have been released between May 8 and August 7, 2026. The archive now includes FBI field reports of triangular craft, Navy footage of airborne anomalies over the Persian Gulf, NASA Apollo crew transcripts, and F-16 gun-camera footage of the February 2023 Lake Huron shootdown. Officials have said releases will continue on a rolling cadence, with a sixth tranche expected within weeks.

On July 31, 2026, the Office of the Director of National Intelligence issued a memo removing all previous non-disclosure agreement barriers for government personnel with knowledge of UAP information — ordering them to report to AARO or PURSUE representatives. Writing on Medium, Harvard astrophysicist Avi Loeb described the memo's significance, noting the memo signed by Principal Deputy Director of National Intelligence Aaron Lukas stated that previous NDAs prohibiting UAP disclosure "are no longer in force."

Despite the volume of released material, the Pentagon's own All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) has been clear about what the files do and do not show. In its Fiscal Year 2025 Consolidated Annual Report — released July 21, 2026, months after its statutory deadline — AARO logged 319 new UAP cases, bringing its total holdings to 1,870 reports since the office's creation. Of those resolved, every case was attributed to conventional objects: balloons, birds, satellites, drones, or aircraft. Nine cases merited further scientific analysis. None of the resolved cases showed advanced foreign adversarial technology or extraterrestrial origin. Close to 200 cases remained unresolved due to insufficient sensor data.

That gap — between the scale of public interest and the official conclusion of "insufficient data" — is precisely the audience SPARK TV is targeting.

Who Built SPARK TV?

Osbourne co-founded SPARK TV with Emmy-nominated filmmaker Serena DC and Michael Mazzola. Serena DC is the founder of Elysium Media, the production company that provides the platform's infrastructure. Mazzola's credentials are notable: he directed two of the most widely viewed UAP documentaries on streaming, "Unacknowledged" and "Close Encounters of the Fifth Kind," and separately co-founded Entangled Labs, a quantum physics research and development company. The founding team's combination of Hollywood production experience and UAP documentary credibility is what distinguishes SPARK TV from a celebrity vanity project.

Osbourne's own paranormal media career spans more than a decade: Haunted Highway (2011–2012), Portals to Hell (2019–2022, Travel Channel), The Osbournes Want to Believe (2020–2021, Travel Channel), and Jack Osbourne's Night of Terror: UFOs (2022). He and Serena DC were also announced as hosts of American Paranormal, an eight-part investigative docuseries for BeaconTV that was in production as of late 2025.

How SPARK TV's Content Model Works

SPARK TV operates as an SVOD (subscription video on demand) platform. The business model, as Serena DC described it, is curation of content the founders own or have licensed — "our own library of stuff that we're interested in" — combined with original productions.

That content strategy was made concrete in April 2026 when SPARK TV signed a 12-show deal with Human Garage, a global self-care movement focused on fascial movement and body awareness, marking the platform's expansion into health, biohacking, and human performance programming. The deal signals that SPARK TV's content model is broader than UFO disclosure alone — Osbourne described it to E! News as covering "yoga meditation stuff, mindfulness stuff. Everything new-agey as well as the paranormal and weird."

The differentiation from generalist platforms like Discovery+ or Max — which both carry paranormal content, including Osbourne's earlier work — lies in the curation framework. SPARK TV positions UAP disclosure, paranormal investigation, and consciousness research as an interconnected subject, not as three separate programming categories. That intellectual through-line is the platform's actual product.

What Is the STEM Case for Consciousness Research?

SPARK TV's inclusion of consciousness studies alongside UAP and paranormal investigation is not arbitrary. It reflects a position held by a growing number of researchers that anomalous phenomena — including UAP encounters, near-death experiences, and claimed extrasensory perception — may require frameworks that go beyond conventional materialist neuroscience to explain.

Philosopher David Chalmers' Hard Problem of Consciousness, introduced in 1995, asks why any physical brain process gives rise to subjective experience at all. No current neuroscientific model fully answers it. Physicist Roger Penrose and anesthesiologist Stuart Hameroff proposed Orchestrated Objective Reduction (Orch-OR), suggesting quantum computations in neural microtubules underlie consciousness — with implications that consciousness may not be fully confined to a biological substrate.

Stanford immunologist Garry Nolan — who has published peer-reviewed research on anomalous materials and testified before Congress on UAP — has argued publicly that consciousness and UAP phenomena may be more deeply connected than standard military intelligence framing suggests. The US government's own STAR GATE program, a $20 million research effort running from 1972 to 1995, funded classified investigation of remote viewing and psychic phenomena; its STARGATE declassified documents are publicly accessible through the CIA FOIA Reading Room.

Whether or not any of these frameworks will ultimately prove correct, they represent a legitimate scientific frontier — which is the audience SPARK TV is explicitly courting.

What the UAP Media Market Looked Like Before SPARK TV

The commercial context matters. In November 2025, "The Age of Disclosure" — a UAP documentary featuring on-record testimony from 34 current and former US government officials, including the former director of the Pentagon's UAP Task Force — landed on Amazon Prime Video. Joe Rogan called it "amazing" and urged major streamers to distribute it widely. It became the highest-grossing documentary of all time on the platform in its initial VOD period, according to reporting.

That success demonstrated an audience for premium UAP content — one that generalist streaming platforms were not specifically built to serve. SPARK TV launches into that demonstrated demand with a team that includes the most credentialed documentary filmmakers in the UAP space.

Osbourne is simultaneously developing an AI-assisted memorial project using Hyperreal's "Digital DNA" technology to create an interactive avatar of his late father, Ozzy Osbourne — a project he announced at Licensing Expo 2026 in Las Vegas and defended publicly against fan criticism in May and June 2026. He is also working on an Ozzy biopic with Sony, with the script complete and a director search underway, as he confirmed to E! News in August 2026. SPARK TV is his primary creative focus right now.

What UAP Audiences Can Actually Watch on SPARK TV Right Now

The platform's curated library covers UAP disclosure, paranormal investigation, consciousness, psychedelics, personal evolution, metaphysical healing, conspiracy, ancient mysteries, biohacking and health, future technology, and what the platform calls "dark investigations." The content is available across web, Amazon, Google Play, and Apple platforms. Jack Osbourne's UFO podcast, which he described as "in the UFO space," has not yet premiered as of late August 2026 but is described as actively in development for the platform.

The broader PURSUE archive — the government's 375 declassified UAP documents — is publicly accessible for free at war.gov/ufo, providing the factual baseline that SPARK TV's commentary and investigative content is designed to frame and contextualize.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is SPARK TV and how do I access it?

SPARK TV (sparktv.ai) is a streaming platform dedicated to UAP disclosure, paranormal investigation, consciousness research, biohacking, and related subjects. It was co-founded by Jack Osbourne, Emmy-nominated filmmaker Serena DC, and documentary filmmaker Michael Mazzola. The platform is available via direct web browser at watch.sparktv.ai and through apps on the Amazon Appstore, Google Play, and Apple platforms. A subscription is required; specific pricing is available at signup.

What UFO files has the US government actually released in 2026?

As of August 2026, the Department of War's PURSUE program has released five tranches of declassified UAP records, totaling 375 documents, videos, and photographs covering cases from 1947 through 2026. The files come from the Pentagon, FBI, CIA, State Department, and Executive Office of the President. AARO — the Pentagon's UAP investigative office — has reviewed 1,870 total cases since 2022 and found no verified evidence of extraterrestrial technology or non-human origin in any resolved case. Hundreds of cases remain unresolved due to insufficient sensor data. A sixth tranche of releases is expected within weeks.

Does Michael Mazzola's background in quantum physics research change what SPARK TV is?

It signals an intention to treat the platform's subject matter with more scientific rigor than the average paranormal entertainment outlet. Mazzola co-founded Entangled Labs, a quantum physics R&D company, in addition to directing major UAP documentaries. That background is relevant when the platform claims to cover "consciousness" and "frontier science" — it means at least one founder has the scientific network and credibility to commission content with genuine research grounding, not just entertainment value.

What is the PURSUE program and why does it matter?

PURSUE — Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters — is the US government's rolling declassification program for UAP-related records, established by Trump executive order in February 2026. On July 31, 2026, the ODNI removed all NDA barriers preventing government personnel from reporting UAP knowledge to authorized channels. PURSUE releases are expected to continue every few weeks. The program represents the largest systematic US government UAP declassification effort since the JFK Records Act. Whether it will eventually confirm non-human technology remains to be seen — AARO's official position is that no resolved case has done so yet.
